tools.name: validate_program
tools.description: Check a program before publishing or saving it: ids, dangling or cyclic triggers, steps overlapping in a track, tasks with no resourceConstraint, durations, replicates/instances misuse. Every finding has a code, a message and a suggested fix. Pure computation.

tools.name: analyze_schedule
tools.description: Put a program on the clock: each step's start and end, total length, the critical path and what gates it, resource conflicts, slack per track. Pass finishAt to answer 'when do I start X so everything is ready at 6pm?'. Pure computation. With `history` (run records) or `program_id` it also predicts d

tools.name: visualize_schedule
tools.description: Publish a program as a live, shareable timeline (a public share link) and return its URL, with an ASCII Gantt and an itinerary. For a schedule the user wants to follow or share ('plan this so it all finishes at 6', 'when do I start each thing'). Validates first and refuses an invalid program with fi

tools.name: import_from_source
tools.description: Import a recipe or protocol from a URL or service into a program. source: spoonacular, themealdb (recipes); protocolsio, opentrons, benchling (lab); cooklang (.cook URL). action: search (no account needed), import (query = URL or id), random. import, random and benchling need the user's Rhylthyme ac

tools.name: import_text
tools.description: Turn pasted text (a recipe, protocol, run sheet or training plan) into a validated multi-track program on the server, in four model turns, with a table of the source span each step came from. Capped per day. Needs the user's Rhylthyme account.

tools.name: create_environment
tools.description: Describe a workspace's equipment limits (one oven, two centrifuges, one stage) as resourceConstraints to copy into a program, so steps that share equipment are scheduled around each other.

tools.name: login
tools.description: For apps that cannot connect the Rhylthyme account directly: returns a sign-in URL, then accepts the pasted token. Only the user's own saved programs, runs and imports need it; everything public works without. Tokens last about an hour.

tools.name: list_my_programs
tools.description: List the user's saved programs. Needs the user's Rhylthyme account.

tools.name: load_program
tools.description: Open one of the user's saved programs by id: summary plus live-timeline URL. Needs the user's Rhylthyme account.

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List recorded runs of a saved program: when, how it ended, actual against planned length. For 'how long did this take last time?'. Needs the user's Rhylthyme account.

tools.name: review_program
tools.description: A model reads an imported program against its source and reports what looks wrong: a default duration on "simmer for an hour", a step the importer dropped, steps chained that could overlap, a total that disagrees with the source. Changes nothing; returns findings to show the user. Needs the user's R

tools.name: load_run
tools.description: Open one recorded run: planned against actual timing per step, what ended each step, pauses. Shows where a plan drifts. Needs the user's Rhylthyme account.

tools.name: calibrate_program
tools.description: Propose durations for a saved program from its recorded runs: median as the default, P10 to P90 as the range, at least as wide as the author's, with the evidence per step and the effect on total length. Saves nothing; with `accept` it returns the calibrated program. Needs the user's Rhylthyme accoun

tools.name: list_public_runs
tools.description: List anonymous runs other people contributed for one exact program version: actual against planned length, and their conditions. For 'how long does this really take?'. No account needed. Takes `program` or `program_hash`.

tools.name: search_public_recipes
tools.description: Search the public catalog of recipes, lab protocols, event templates and workouts by name or keyword. Returns ids, names, descriptions and URLs; no account needed.

tools.name: load_public_recipe
tools.description: Open a public catalog entry by id: summary plus live-timeline URL.

tools.name: save_program
tools.description: Save a program to the user's account ('save this for later'); the same programId updates it. Needs the user's Rhylthyme account.

tools.name: preview_timeline
tools.description: Return a static Gantt image of a program with a caption, for 'show me a preview' or 'a picture of the timeline'. The image is served from a public share link. Planned versus actual: with `run` (a run record) it draws the actual bars over the plan.

tools.name: get_renderer_source
tools.description: Return the open-source timeline renderer's JavaScript (Apache-2.0, about 90 KB, no dependencies) for an HTML page or artifact that cannot load external scripts; it defines Rhylthyme.renderTimeline(container, program).

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "search_public_recipes" appears informational but accepts parameters (environment) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: query, environment, limit

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_program, import_from_source, load_program, search_public_recipes, load_public_recipe, get_renderer_source · Private data: analyze_schedule, login, preview_timeline · Public sink: visualize_schedule, create_environment, preview_timeline · Destructive: analyze_schedule, import_text, load_run, preview_timeline.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_program, import_from_source, load_program, search_public_recipes, load_public_recipe, get_renderer_source · Private data: analyze_schedule, login, preview_timeline · Public sink: visualize_schedule, create_environment, preview_timeline · Destructive: analyze_schedule, import_text, load_run, preview_timeline

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
